changeSet.author: bng-team
changeSet.comment: Create login_audit table: an append-only record of every successful user login. One row is written by the application (POST /auth/login-audit) per login, from the verified Defra ID token claims. logged_in_at defaults to now() and is stored in UTC (timestamptz).

changeSet.author: bng-team
changeSet.comment: Index login_audit by user_id for efficient per-user login history lookups

changeSet.author: bng-team
changeSet.comment: Make bng.login_audit append-only. Rows are written once per login and nothing ever legitimately updates or deletes a login-audit row. Guard the table at the database level so no role can edit, delete or bulk-wipe history: a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE row-level trigger and a BEFORE TRUNCATE statement-level trigger both raise insufficient_privilege. INSERT is left untouched, so logins keep being recorded. This holds for every role — including the application role and the table owner — regardless of how table privileges are granted; the only way past it is to drop or disable the trigger, which is a deploy-time DDL action. Mirrors the bng.audit_log guard in db.changelog-1.9.xml.

changeSet.author: bng-team
changeSet.comment: Least-privilege backstop for the append-only guard: revoke the mutating privileges on bng.login_audit from PUBLIC so no role inherits them by default. Non-application ("read-only") roles must be granted SELECT only; the application role needs SELECT, INSERT and never UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE. Per-role grants are provisioned by CDP infrastructure outside this changelog (see docs/DATABASE.md — Audit Log Immutability); this REVOKE ensures the default state is closed. Rollback is intentionally empty: PUBLIC holds none of these privileges by default, so there is nothing to restore.
changeSet.sql: REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON bng.login_audit FROM PUBLIC;

changeSet.author: bng-team
changeSet.comment: Enforce one login_audit row per session with a unique constraint on session_id. The login is recorded as part of the POST /auth/session workflow, which appends with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — so a repeat /auth/session call for an already-recorded session is a graceful no-op, not an error, and the table records distinct logins rather than endpoint calls. NULL session_ids are distinct under standard Postgres semantics, so a login whose token carries no session id is always recorded (it cannot be de-duplicated). ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (never DO UPDATE) keeps this compatible with the append-only guard, which rejects UPDATE. Liquibase auto-generates the drop rollback.
